root_cause.text: libie_fwlog_deinit() in the Intel libie fwlog subsystem assumed firmware logging had been initialized and performed teardown on an unsupported/unconfigured fwlog object, leading to invalid device access during driver unload.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an early `if (!libie_fwlog_supported(fwlog)) return;` guard in `drivers/net/ethernet/intel/libie/fwlog.c`, and the commit/CVE explicitly state that `libie_fwlog_deinit()` could be called "even when firmware logging was never properly initialized," causing an Oops in `_dev_warn`/`__dev_printk` from `libie_fwlog_deinit`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a support check in firmware log deinit so cleanup is skipped when firmware logging was never configured.
intent_record.what: A new early-return check was added at the start of libie_fwlog_deinit() that calls libie_fwlog_supported(fwlog) and returns immediately if firmware logging is not supported, along with a comment explaining that no configuration would have been done in that case.
intent_record.how: At runtime, deinitialization now skips the firmware logging teardown path on devices or configurations where firmware logging is unsupported, preventing unnecessary or invalid disable/configuration actions during cleanup.

grouping_result.intent: Add a support check in firmware log deinit so cleanup is skipped when firmware logging was never configured.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by adding a guard in firmware log deinit to skip teardown when fwlog was never configured/supported, preventing invalid access during driver unload.

The root cause is the lack of a guard for unsupported/uninitialized firmware logging before performing cleanup, but the actual teardown statements are not present in the provided pre-fix lines. This line identifies the function body but is not itself the direct faulty operation.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it directly shows the teardown logic in question. The vulnerable construct is present: the function unconditionally proceeds with FW log teardown after only checking `if (hw->bus.func) return;` on lines 50-52. It then assumes FW logging was configured/initialized and modifies `hw->fwlog_cfg.options` on line 57, calls `ice_fwlog_set(hw, &hw->fwlog_cfg);` on line 58, and frees `pf->ice_debugfs_pf_fwlog_modules` on line 63. There is no guard checking whether FW logging was actually initialized/supported/configured before attempting this teardown. That matches the root cause: `libie_fwlog_deinit()` assumes firmware logging had been initialized and performs teardown on an unsupported/unconfigured fwlog object. No fix is present in this snippet, because there is no conditional such as an initialized/supported flag check before disabling FW logging or freeing associated resources.
